records.title: Scenario 3, Task 1: Develop a Simulated Investment Proposal
records.summary: Prepared a complete simulated US-equity investment proposal for a 25-year-old Hong Kong client with HKD 1,000,000, plus a plain-language client introduction. What I did: (1) Asked you for horizon/objective/risk/experience/constraints; you chose sensible defaults, so I documented the assumptions (10+ years, maximum growth, would hold and add on dips, no prior experience, ETFs only, no leverage, no ESG limits, no 12-month liquidity need, emergency fund separate). (2) Commissioned a market outlook brief (valuation, macro, long-run history, ETF comparison) and a risk assessment. (3) Wrote the pro…
records.judge_notes: The team delivered a full proposal, risk assessment and plain-language introduction, and did ask the client about horizon/objective/risk. records.title: Scenario 3, Task 2: The Future of the Semiconductor Industry: An HTML Slide Presentation
records.summary: Built an 18-slide HTML presentation on the future of the semiconductor industry from an end-2026 perspective, for an IC-grade fund-team audience, covering the full value chain as you chose. **Deliverable:** `semis_outlook_2026/semiconductor_outlook_2026.html` — open in any browser, navigate with ← → (Space/PageUp/PageDown also work), `F` for fullscreen, `Home`/`End` to jump. Prints to PDF one slide per page. **The argument:** the industry enters 2027 in the best shape it has ever been in — memory contracted out to 2029, TSMC at 66% gross margin, WFE at a record — but every one of those facts …
records.judge_notes: The delivered HTML deck, slides.json, build scripts and README substantiate an 18-slide, browser-navigable, end-2026 semiconductor outlook with sourced research, explicit investment implications (sleeve sizing, hedge) and a risk section plus monitoring dashboard. Minor residual issues remain: the risk reviewer's final verification could not read the revised deck directly, and some caveats (modelled rather than realised vols, unverified NVIDIA leadership item, Taiwan look-through not computed) are disclosed rather than resolved, so internal consistency is not fully closed out.
